conviction_note: Choice last spoke on 2026-08-05 and implied Q3 U.S. RevPAR only 'a little stronger' than an H2 guide of about +1.5%, with Q4 moderating. Since then its closest peer, Wyndham, printed U.S. RevPAR +6% (economy +5%, midscale +6%) with October running at the same pace, and Hilton printed U.S. +7%. So a RevPAR beat and a full-year RevPAR/EBITDA raise are likely. Against that: the stock is already +8.5% over 20 days; consensus EPS ($2.26 for Q3, $7.14 for the year) already sits above the top of guidance ($7.10); a $9.5m liquidated-damages item in last year's Q3 does not recur; and interest expense keeps the EPS guide tight. Short interest is about 12.8 days to cover, which gives a beat more room to run. So p_up is 58 on abs_move 5.5 (= +0.88), while the findings sum to +2.0. The gap is the run-up and the above-guide consensus, which pull p_up toward 50 but do not shrink the peer finding itself.

findings.finding: Wyndham, Choice's closest economy/midscale franchisor peer, reported on 2026-10-21 (after Choice last spoke on 08-05). Its Q3 U.S. RevPAR was +6% y/y to $58.35: economy +5% to $48.58, midscale/upper midscale +6% to $66.09. Wyndham said October was running about the same as Q3 and assumes Q4 domestic RevPAR stays in line with Q3. Choice's own guide implies Q3 U.S. RevPAR only 'a little stronger' than the ~+1.5% H2 guide (July was +100bp vs June), with Q4 moderating, inside an FY range of 0% to +1.25%. Choice lagged Wyndham by ~70bp in Q2 (+1.3% vs +2%), and the two-year stacks (Wyndham Q3'25 -5%, Choice Q3'25 -3.2%) point to Choice Q3 U.S. RevPAR of roughly +3% to +4.5%. That is 1-3 points above its own implied Q3, and it points to a raise of the FY U.S. RevPAR and EBITDA guide, with Q4 upside against a guide that assumed moderation. Hilton (U.S. +7%, 10-27) and CoStar's weekly data (U.S. RevPAR +14.2% in the week to 09-26, partly a Rosh Hashanah shift) say the same, but those are upscale/industry-wide. Choice said on the Q2 call that it is under-indexed in urban and business-transient markets, which led the rebound, so this is sized net of a capture gap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-05: EBITDA and U.S. RevPAR guide raised, EPS guide trimmed: +2.93%. 2025-11-05: U.S. RevPAR -3.2% and EPS missed, yet the stock rose +5.98%. 2026-04-30: Q1 EPS miss, guide only held: -15.58%. RevPAR/guide surprises have moved this name 3-6% with one large downside tail.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. CHH is +8.5% over 20 days, which covers the WH (10-21) and HLT (10-27) prints, and FY EPS consensus ($7.14) already sits above the guide top. But the guide still reads 0% to +1.25% U.S. RevPAR, and Q3 consensus revenue is +1.7% y/y ($454.9m). A Street fully marked to a ~4% RevPAR quarter would carry revenue growth nearer 3% and an FY EPS above $7.20. The 5.5% event-implied move shows the market is not positioned for a one-sided outcome.
findings.independence: Hilton Q3 2026 U.S. RevPAR +7%, FY RevPAR raised to 4-4.5% (https://www.hoteldive.com/news/hilton-raises-full-year-revpar-outlook-after-strong-q3/872934/, 2026-10-27). CoStar weekly U.S. RevPAR +14.2% for the week to 2026-09-26 (https://www.hotel-online.com/news/us-hotel-industry-posts-strong-gains-as-revpar-jumps-142, 2026-10-05). Both are different documents but the same underlying fact (strong U.S. Q3 lodging demand), so they are merged here rather than filed twice. Choice's own guide comes from its Q2 call transcript (the bar).

findings.finding: Q2 call: FY adj. EPS guide cut to $6.86-7.10 'primarily reflecting higher expected interest expense and a higher effective tax rate.' Since then Choice signed a $500m unsecured term loan (8-K, 2026-08-28; SOFR+125) and on 2026-09-30 agreed a ~$130m all-cash Harvest Hosts acquisition funded from cash and the revolver, 'not material' to 2026. With FY EPS consensus (~$7.14) above the guide top, an operating raise that leaves the EPS range flat or trimmed (interest, tax, a non-hotel deal) reads as a below-Street EPS guide. On what the money buys: buybacks ($175-225m planned for 2026), the Harvest Hosts deal and refinancing, not distress (net leverage 3.1x, inside the 3-4x target). So this is sized as a bar risk on the EPS line, not as a financing negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-05: EPS guide trimmed while EBITDA was raised; the stock rose +2.93%, so the EPS trim was looked through once. 2026-04-30: EPS miss with guidance held: -15.58%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $7.14 against a $7.10 guide top suggests the Street already assumes a raise. A flat EPS range would be a visible miss against that, and nothing in the price (+8.5% run-up) allows for it. Shrunk for the crowded short.

baseline_tension: The evidence points up, but the +8.5% 20-day run-up and an EPS consensus already above guidance show part of the peer read-through is priced. There is no skew number to cut against, and the put/call OI ratio sits on 139 contracts, so it says nothing. The crowded short (12.8 days) adds upside convexity; that is why p_up stays at 58 instead of the low 60s that the peer evidence alone would justify.
lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the term loan and Harvest Hosts were asked what they buy (buybacks, a small deal, refi; leverage 3.1x inside target). Refiled from a financing negative to an EPS-guide bar risk and shrunk from -0.8 to -0.4, also per lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative).
Lesson 6 (inside what the company guided): the $9.5m liquidated-damages lap was flagged by the company, so it moved toward 0, from -0.3 to -0.1.

'What has worked' (a peer print after the company last spoke leaves consensus stale): the Wyndham finding was kept at +1.5 with lands_on guidance and not shrunk further; the under-indexing caveat was already netted in once.
p_up raised from 57 to 58: with the negatives shrunk, the scaled number went from +0.77 to +0.88. abs_move unchanged at 5.5.
